module_title: State Legislature - Composition, Elections, and Creation/Abolition
introduction: At this level, we explore the constitutional process of creating or abolishing a Legislative Council, the maximum and minimum strength limits for both houses, and the complex fractional election process for MLCs.

core_concepts.title: Creation or Abolition of the Council (Article 169)
core_concepts.description: Parliament can create or abolish a Legislative Council by a simple law, BUT this can only happen if the Legislative Assembly of that state first passes a resolution to that effect by a 'Special Majority' (2/3rd of members present and voting).

core_concepts.title: Strength of the Houses
core_concepts.description: Legislative Assembly: Maximum 500, Minimum 60 members. Legislative Council: Maximum 1/3rd of the total strength of the state's Assembly, but it cannot be less than 40 members.

core_concepts.title: Composition of the Legislative Council
core_concepts.description: MLCs are chosen in 5 ways: 1/3rd elected by local bodies (municipalities, etc.), 1/3rd by MLAs, 1/12th by graduates of 3 years standing, 1/12th by teachers of 3 years standing, and the remaining 1/6th are nominated by the Governor.

core_concepts.title: Governor's Nomination
core_concepts.description: The Governor nominates 1/6th of the MLCs from people having special knowledge in 5 fields: Literature, Science, Art, Cooperative Movement, and Social Service.

important_entities.name: The Parliament
important_entities.description: Even if a State Assembly passes a resolution to create a Council, the ultimate power to actually create it lies exclusively with the Parliament.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: While the Constitution sets the minimum Assembly strength at 60, there are exceptions for smaller states due to special provisions: Sikkim (32), Mizoram (40), and Goa (40).

The President nominates members to the Rajya Sabha from 4 fields (Art, Literature, Science, Social Service). However, the Governor nominates members to the Legislative Council from 5 fields (the 5th being 'Cooperative Movement').

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: 1/3 (MLAs), 1/3 (Local Bodies), 1/6 (Governor), 1/12 (Graduates), 1/12 (Teachers). Adding these fractions together equals 1 (the whole house).

exam_strategy_tips: Article 169 (Creation and Abolition of Legislative Councils) is one of the most frequently asked articles in State PCS exams.
Be prepared for 'Match the Following' questions regarding the fractions of the Legislative Council's electoral college (e.g., matching 1/12 to Teachers/Graduates).
